headline: Updates on high school construction covered water seepage, roof water damage, and a $418 million budget; no votes were recorded.
summary: The meeting covered construction progress, a plan to stop water seepage at the East Campus buildings, and the project budget. Members asked about roof water damage and mold checks. No votes were recorded.
discussion: East Campus water seepage: A consultant said water from rain and watering gets into the unprotected 1922 and 1892 basement walls, not water from the Merrimack Canal. The plan adds waterproofing and drainage on the west and south sides. Members asked about keeping water away from the building on the east side.

Roof water damage: Rain came through an opening in the roof in October. The contractor said the damaged materials will be removed and replaced, and that two inspections will confirm they are dry before new materials go in. Members asked who pays, whether the schedule will slip, and how repeat leaks will be prevented.

Construction budget: About $8.6 million remained in construction contingency, with $8.9 million in pending change requests. Officials said those figures are estimates that could rise or fall as work continues.
Fire pump: Officials said the fire pump is part of a fix for the attic sprinkler system, and that the engineering is still being finalized. A cost summary was expected the following week.
